title: Isaac Mizrahi on the ‘Unzipped’ Restoration, the John Galliano Met Gala Fiasco and Why the ‘Devil Wears Prada’ Cerulean Blue Speech ‘Makes Me Want to Kill Somebody’
content:
The designer and entertainer also reveals that he's developing a TV series with producer Christine Vachon about the late paparazzi photographer Ron Galella.

ByMarc Malkin

Senior Editor, Culture and Events

No doubtIsaac Mizrahiis excited about the release of the newly restored “Unzipped,” the 1995 documentary chronicling a moment in time when he was one of the fashion world’s hottest designers.

However, Mizrahi admits he’s not that eager to watch it. “I have to say I hate looking back,” he tells me. “I hate this whole process, a little bit of looking back.”

What’s so wrong with taking a trip down memory lane?

“I looked so cute, and I look so shitty now,” the 64-year-old Mizrahi says. “I was so agile, and I’m not as agile anymore. My knees hurt. My back hurts. Even my hair. I had such cute dark hair. Oh, well. But it’s not just vanity. It’s more just about the experience of your life. Thirty years! Man, that is crazy.”

Directed by Mizarahi’s then-boyfriend Douglas Keeves, “Unzipped” chronicles the designer’s planning and execution of the show for his fall 1994 collection.

The film, which Miramax bought after it was a Sundance hit in 1995, includes appearances by Cindy Crawford, Linda Evangelista, Naomi Campbell, Kate Moss, the late André Leon Talley and Eartha Kitt along with a bevy of other fashion insiders and glitterati.

The film runs at only 73 minutes. “We didn’t intend to make it that short,” Mizrahi remembers. “We wanted it to be longer. There were about 10 minutes of Faye Dunaway that got out because we couldn’t get the rights to run footage from ‘Mommy Dearest.’”

What?!

“She came to a fitting. She was doing a TV pilot, and she needed a lot of suits,” Mizrahi remembers. “We had her for a day and a half, a fitting that was endless. Being the big gay that I am, I was enthralled by every word out of her mouth. One really hilarious thing that I do remember about Faye Dunaway was that she would look in the mirror, and when she liked something, she’d go, ‘Oh, that’s very Faye. Very Faye.’ Talking about herself in the third person was so fantastic. And I do that now. If I like what I look like, I go, ‘Oh, it’s very Faye.’ It’s like I think of myself as Faye Dunaway.”

I ask Mizrahi what he would tell himself if he could go back three decades. Without missing a beat, he says, “’You’re not that fat!’ Swear to God, that’s what I would tell myself. I used to wear these crazy Fred Mertz kind of high-waisted pleated pants that I made myself because I was so fucking crazy that my waist was big. I was so stupid, and I look stupid, I don’t look chic. I look stupid, and I was perfectly fine. I was not fat. But I was a really fat kid, so I lost 75 pounds in high school. I’m never going to get over that. You never do.”

Mizrahi makes no secret about being on a GLP-1. “I love it,” he coos. “I’m in my 60s, darling and I recently just got so big. I’m usually very good at keeping it under control, but it’s incredible and the rest of your health benefits, it’s incredible.”

At the height of releasing his eponymous collection, he dressed the A-list, including Sarah Jessica Parker, Nicole Kidman and Natalie Portman. After closing shop in 1998, he released various collections under different monikers or designed for other brands altogether. He also launched a show business career with a cabaret act. Most recently, he appeared in “Marty Supreme” as Gwyneth Paltrow’s press agent.

Mizrahi is now the creative director at Target and continues to sell a collection on QVC.

When talking about fashion today, Mizrahi lets out a big sigh. “I don’t know if those giant spectacles they have in Paris and Milan are necessarily supposed to be influential in the way people dress six months later,” he says. “That is why that speech in ‘The Devil Wears Prada’ about cerulean blue makes me want to kill somebody because that is so not the way things work. They want you to believe that’s the way it works. I want to shout that from the rooftops, ‘It never has worked that way — never!’” What those spectacles do is they bolster the image of brand names so that they can sell a ton of perfume and handbags and shoes.”

When we talked, it was just a few days after The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced it was no longer moving forward with its planned retrospective forJohn Gallianothat would’ve run from May 9, 2027, to Jan. 9, 2028 and served as the theme of next year’sMet Gala. Galliano, who would have been only the third living fashion designer to be feted by the Met following Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo in 2017, released a statement on Instagram announcing his decision to pull the retrospective amid backlash over his past racist outbursts.

Galliano makes a brief appearance in “Unzipped” at dinner with Mizrahi, Talley and others in Paris. Mizrahi calls Galliano a “genius,” but also says, “When they announced [the Galliano Met Gala], I thought to myself, ‘Wow, who’s going to that?’ I’m not even talking about Jews or donors of the museum. I’m thinking about a celebrity showing up. I don’t know who would show up on that red carpet. No one is going to say, ‘I love John.’ Who’s going to say that?”

Next up could for Mizrahi could be a producer’s hat. He’s developing a television series about the life of legendary and very controversial paparazzi photographer Ron Galella with producer Christine Vachon. “We’re doing it with the Ron Galella estate,” he says. “It’s very exciting. We’re in the first, first, first stages, so we haven’t even pitched it or anything yet. But it’s really such a great idea, only because of what it means culturally to our country.”

“Unzipped” is now showing at the Film Forum in New York City. It will open in Los Angeles at Laemmle Royal and Laemmle Glendale on Oct. 9, followed by a nationwide rollout.
title_zh: 艾薩克·米茲拉希(Issac Mizrahi)談論《Unzipped》修復、約翰·加利亞諾(John Galliano)的Met Gala災難，以及為什麼《穿著普拉達的惡魔》(The Devil Wears Prada)中的天藍色演講讓他「想要殺人」。
content_zh:
設計師兼娛樂人員艾薩克·米茲拉希(Ike Mizrahi)也透露，他正在與製片人克里斯汀·瓦喬(Christine Vachon)合作開發一部關於已故狗仔攝影師羅恩·加雷拉(Ron Galella)的電視劇。

由馬克·馬爾金(Marc Malkin)報導

文化與活動資深編輯

毫無疑問，艾薩克·米茲拉希(Ike Mizrahi)對於新修復的紀錄片《Unzipped》感到興奮，這部1995年的紀錄片記錄了他作為時尚界最炙手可熱的設計師之一的那段時光。

然而，米茲拉希坦言他並不太想觀看這部影片。“我必須說，我討厭回顧過去，”他告訴我。“我討厭這整個過程，稍微回顧一下。”

回憶往昔有什麼錯呢？

“我那時候看起來好可愛，而現在看起來糟透了，”64歲的米茲拉希說。“我那時候多麼靈活，而現在不再那麼靈活了。我的膝蓋疼，我的背也疼。甚至我的頭髮。我曾經有多麼可愛的深色頭髮。哦，好吧。但這不只是虛榮。更多的是關於你生活的經歷。三十年！天啊，這真瘋狂。”

《Unzipped》由米茲拉希當時的男友道格拉斯·基夫斯(Douglas Keeves)執導，紀錄了設計師為1994年秋季系列秀的策劃與執行。

這部影片在1995年於聖丹斯影展大獲成功後被米拉麥克斯(Miramax)購得，影片中出現了辛迪·克勞馥(Cindy Crawford)、琳達·伊凡傑莉斯塔(Linda Evangelista)、娜奧米·坎貝爾(Naomi Campbell)、凱特·摩斯(Kate Moss)、已故的安德烈·里昂·塔利(André Leon Talley)和厄莎·基特(Eartha Kitt)，以及一眾時尚界內部人士和名流。

影片僅有73分鐘長。“我們並不打算讓它那麼短，”米茲拉希回憶道。“我們希望它更長。大約有10分鐘的費伊·鄧威(Faye Dunaway)的片段因為我們無法獲得《媽媽親愛的》(Mommy Dearest)的播放權而被刪除。”

什麼？！

“她來參加了一次試衣。她正在拍攝一部電視試播集，需要很多西裝，”米茲拉希回憶道。“我們有她一天半，試衣的時間無窮無盡。作為一個大同性戀者，我被她口中的每一句話迷住了。我記得有一件非常搞笑的事情是，費伊·鄧威會看著鏡子，當她喜歡某樣東西時，她會說，‘哦，這非常費伊。非常費伊。’用第三人稱談論自己真是太棒了。而我現在也這樣做。如果我喜歡我自己的樣子，我會說，‘哦，這非常費伊。’就像我把自己想成費伊·鄧威。”

我問米茲拉希，如果他能回到三十年前，他會告訴自己什麼。毫不猶豫地，他說：“‘你並沒有那麼胖！’我發誓，這就是我會告訴自己的話。我曾經穿著那些瘋狂的弗雷德·梅茨(Fred Mertz)式高腰褶皺褲子，因為我太瘋狂了，所以我的腰圍很大。我真是太傻了，我看起來傻，我看起來不時尚。我看起來傻，但我當時完全沒問題。我並不胖。但我是一個非常胖的小孩，所以我在高中減掉了75磅。我永遠無法克服這一點。你永遠也不會。”

米茲拉希(Ibrahim Mizrahi)對於自己正在使用GLP-1藥物毫不避諱。他滿心歡喜地說：“我愛它。親愛的，我已經60多歲了，最近變得非常胖。我通常很擅長控制體重，但這真的太不可思議了，還有其他健康益處，真是太驚人了。”

在推出以自己名字命名的系列的巔峰時期，他為許多A-list明星設計服裝，包括莎拉·潔西卡·帕克(Sarah Jessica Parker)、妮可·基嫚(Nicole Kidman)和娜塔莉·波特曼(Natalie Portman)。1998年關閉工作室後，他以不同的名字推出了各種系列，或為其他品牌設計。他還以一場歌舞表演開始了自己的演藝事業。最近，他在《馬提·超級明星(Marty Supreme)》中出現，擔任格温妮絲·帕特洛(Gwyneth Paltrow)的公關代理。

目前，米茲拉希是Target的創意總監，並繼續在QVC上銷售他的系列產品。

談到當今的時尚時，米茲拉希發出一聲長嘆。“我不知道他們在巴黎和米蘭舉辦的那些大型活動是否真的會對人們六個月後的穿著產生影響，”他說。“這就是為什麼《穿著Prada的惡魔(The Devil Wears Prada)》中關於天藍色的演講讓我想殺人的原因，因為這根本不是事情的運作方式。他們想讓你相信這就是運作的方式。我想從屋頂上大喊，‘這從來都不是這樣運作的——從來沒有！’”這些大型活動的作用是提升品牌形象，以便他們能賣出大量香水、手袋和鞋子。

我們交談的時候，正好是在大都會藝術博物館(The Metropolitan Museum of Art)宣布不再推進約翰·嘉利亞諾(John Galliano)的回顧展計劃幾天後，該展覽原定於2027年5月9日至2028年1月9日舉行，並作為明年Met Gala的主題。嘉利亞諾將成為繼1983年的伊夫·聖羅蘭(Yves Saint Laurent)和2017年的川久保玲(Rei Kawakubo)之後，第三位受到大都會藝術博物館讚譽的在世時尚設計師，他在Instagram上發表聲明，宣布因對他過去的種族主義言論的反彈而決定撤回回顧展。

嘉利亞諾在《未解之謎(Unzipped)》中短暫出現，與米茲拉希、塔利(Talley)和其他人在巴黎共進晚餐。米茲拉希稱嘉利亞諾為“天才”，但也說：“當他們宣布[嘉利亞諾Met Gala]時，我心想，‘哇，誰會去呢？’我甚至不是在談論猶太人或博物館的捐贈者。我在想的是會有名人出現。我不知道誰會在那條紅地毯上出現。沒有人會說，‘我愛約翰。’誰會這麼說？”

接下來，米茲拉希可能會戴上製片人的帽子。他正在與製片人克里斯汀·瓦喬(Christine Vachon)開發一部關於傳奇且極具爭議的狗仔攝影師羅恩·加萊拉(Ron Galella)生活的電視劇。“我們正在與羅恩·加萊拉的遺產合作，”他說。“這非常令人興奮。我們正處於第一、第一、第一階段，所以我們甚至還沒有推銷它或其他任何事情。但這真的是一個很棒的主意，因為它對我們國家的文化意義。”

《解開(Unzipped)》目前正在紐約市的電影論壇放映。它將於10月9日在洛杉磯的Laemmle Royal和Laemmle Glendale上映，隨後將在全國範圍內推廣。
summary_zh: 設計師兼娛樂人員艾薩克·米茲拉希(Ike Mizrahi)也透露，他正在與製片人克里斯汀·瓦喬(Christine Vachon)合作開發一部關於已故狗仔攝影師羅恩·加雷拉(Ron Galella)的電視劇。
